newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices end up 1/2 to 5/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices end up 1/2 to 5/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended 1/2 to 5/8 of a point higher Thursday amid bidlists totaling $500 million to $600 million by one estimate.

"There have been a lot of lists the last two or three days, not a lot of volume in any one list, but a lot smaller lists mostly paying for new issues," one trader said. The lists were getting bids, he said.
A second trader said few of the lists offered bonds in the serial range.
"It was mostly long end selling," he said.
The trader estimated that lists totaled $200 million to $250 million. A municipal analyst cited more volume, estimating the lists' par value at $500 million to $600 million.

As for Thursday's price action, high-grade issues improved by five basis points, the analyst said, while dollar bonds were up about 5/8 point. The secondary market was active and new issue pricing was "very strong" on the long end, he said.
In competitive action, Merrill Lynch & Co won $250 million Florida Board of Education public education capital outlay bonds with a true interest cost of 5.571 percent.
A Merrill Lynch & Co source said the deal went "very well," with just $2.2 million left near day's end.

"I tell you, it surprised a lot of people, especially given the run in the market," the source said, adding that some players felt the market may have gone up too far too fast. "But you know we've got a $2 million balance."
Merrill saw "right at the bell, a substantial amount of pre-sale institutional business" in the form of insurance companies, bond funds and money managers, he said.

"And then we had a nice follow through afterwards, so it's a very nice deal, and I think a lot of people are fairly positive about the market given those numbers that came out this morning," the source said.

The Commerce Department reported that durable goods orders fell 3.1 percent in August after rising a revised 1.4 percent in July. Also, the U.S. Labor Department reported that jobless claims rose to 340,000 for the week ended September 21, up from 329,00 the previous week.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 19/32 at 114-17/32. The December T-bond contract was up 19/32 at 109-26/32. The MOB spread was 151 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 17/32 at 98-9/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
